title.narrative: OHCHR (UNJHRO) DRK, programme support 2022-2024 - OHCHR UNJHRO DRC, programme support 2022-2024

description.narrative:
Pillar 1. Strengthening rule of law and accountability for human rights violations
Pillar 1 result: Laws, policies, and practices increasingly address, prevent and reduce human rights violations in the context of law enforcement and justice systems
Country result: Increased number of convictions by the judiciary and or disciplinary measures taken by oversight mechanisms in response to human rights violations including sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV)
Output 1: Increased number of convictions on emblematic cases of grave human rights violations.
Output 2: The legal framework is improved making the justice system more compliant with the Constitution and international human rights instruments ratified by DRC
Output 3: Strengthened capacity of the Government to further implement the agreed frameworks on addressing sexual violence crimes and improved UN coordination and response to conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV)
Pillar 2. Enhancing and Protecting Civic Space and Peoples Participation
Pillar 2 result 1: Stronger laws, policies and practices protect the right to participate and civic space, including online, and the environment for civil society is increasingly safe and enabling
Country Result: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is more effective in fulfilling its mandate in accordance with the Paris Principles, including in handling complaints
Output 1: Reinforced capacities of NHRI to better fulfil its mandate within all the DRC, including complaints handling, and its role in protecting human rights. Improved abilities of the HR Defenders and Protection Networks to support NHRI work in safeguarding human rights and in enhancing their autonomy.
Output 2: Improved abilities of the HR Defenders and Protection Networks to support NHRI work in safeguarding human rights and in enhancing their autonomy.
Pillar 2 result 2: Civil society assistance to victims of human rights violations (HRV) is strengthened
Country Result: Increased number of victims of human rights violations benefiting from assistance by the civil society networks supported by the UNJHRO
Output 1: Improved knowledge and skills of civil society networks on protective measures and mechanisms in assisting victims of human rights violations.
Output 2: Increased awareness of parliamentarians and governmental authorities on legal mechanisms in preventing and protecting victims of human rights violations, including through adoption of laws on protection HRD, access to information and right to peaceful demonstrations which are aligned with international human rights standards
Pillar 2 result 3: More systematic monitoring of the environment for civic space, including threats to it, takes place
Country Result: Better respect of human rights norms, standards and principles by the security forces in the context of the exercise by the citizens of the rights to freedom of expression, assembly and association
Output 2: Progress towards an environment more conducive to a consolidated participatory democracy (Shift: Civic Space).
Pillar 3. Enhancing equality and countering discrimination
Pillar 3 result: Laws, policies, and practices more effectively combat discrimination in all forms, and responsible authorities actively work to 'leave no one behind', including by addressing the root causes of inequality
Output 1: Advocacy sessions towards national institutions responsible for legislative action to address protection gaps for vulnerable groups (especially women, girls and indigenous people)
Output 2: Enhanced justice for and socio-economic reintegration of vulnerable groups, including displaced people; strengthened ability to claim and advocate for the rights of vulnerable groups and urging governmental actors to act upon it, notably in the Grand Kasai
Output 3: Increased awareness, expanded knowledge, use of HRBA and on vulnerable groups rights to be used by the JHRO staff and Human Rights NGOs for reporting to HR Mechanisms, Bodies and the UPR
Pillar 4. Integrating human rights in sustainable development
Pillar 4 result: Human rights assessments and impact analyses mitigate, prevent or redress the negative effects of economic, trade and development policies and projects
Output 1: Increased awareness, understanding and respect of civil society (marginalized groups) on economic, social and cultural rights (ESC) and business and HR principles.
Output 2: Improved data collection on ESC rights violations and creation and functioning of a framework protecting economic and social rights
Output 3: Alignment of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF, ex-UNDAF) indicators and targets with the human rights recommendations and the SDGs
Pillar 5. Early warning, prevention, and protection of human rights in situations of conflict and insecurity
Pillar 5 result 1: Human rights information and analyses are integrated in early warning and analysis systems and influence international and national policymaking, strategies and operations to prevent, mitigate or respond to emerging crises, including humanitarian crises and conflict.
Country Result: Increased number of the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy (HRDDP) related risk assessment resulting in the adoption of mitigation or correctives measures by the security forces.
Output 1: Increased number of measures taken to address HRV committed by the DRC security forces.
Output 2: Improved tools provided to the State Authorities to prevent Human Rights violations, protect civilians and improve fight against impunity, including increased accountability of State Agents.
Output 3: Substantive information relating to human rights violations perpetrated by the DRC's Security Forces or by armed groups is converted into actionable analysis, informs programming and is disseminated to relevant stakeholder
Output 4: Knowledge and awareness of the HRDDP has increased among UNCT and Congolese partners and inform programs and projects.
Output 5: National DDR-like processes (e.g. Spontaneous demobilization and surrendering of armed groups and reintegration) are subject to the HRDDP and compliant to International Human rights Standards
Pillar 5 result 2: United Nations' support to national and regional security forces, law enforcement agencies, and non-State actors integrates human rights and complies with the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy
Country Result: Decision making process within MONUSCO in support to the political process and to POC is fully guided by the relevant human rights norms, standards and principles especially through the good offices of the mission leadership or in the context of the provision of support to the security forces
Output 1: Increased compliance of the mission interventions in the context of the implementation of the mandate with the human rights norms, principles and standards
Output 2: Improved understanding of PoC by National security agencies, local communities and civil society in areas of conflict, favouring greater collaboration between actors
Pillar 6. Increasing implementation of the international human rights mechanisms' outcomes
Pillar 6 result 1: National institutionalized structures facilitate an integrated and participatory approach to reporting to the human rights mechanisms and implementation of their recommendations.
Country Result: The existing inter-ministerial committee on reporting to the Treaty Bodies becomes permanent and functional
Output 1: Strengthened capacity of the Committees members to fulfil their mandate.
Pillar 6 result 2: Civil society organizations, national human rights institutions, and non-traditional actors, particularly those working on emerging human rights issues (frontier issues), increasingly engage with the international human rights mechanisms and use their outcomes
Country Result: NHRC and other active HRD NGOs increase their contributions and submissions to the international human rights mechanism regarding serious human rights issues in DRC
Output 1: Improved capacities of the NHRC and civil society organizations and networks to make submission to human rights mechanisms. Increased participation to the follow up on the implementation of the recommendations of the human rights recommendations, including the Universal Periodic Review

UNJHRO (JHRO) monitors the human rights situation in the DRC and Sweden has been supporting their office bilaterally since 2016 with two different contributions. According to the embassy, and the international community at large in DRC, the JHRO is the strongest human rights actor in DRC and therefore the embassy wants to support the office. The JHRO is a joint office between the OHCHR and the human rights section of the Monusco mission in DRC. In addition JHRO is working closely with UNDP in providing training in human rights to the Army and the Police and they are also closely connected in the take-over in the withdrawal of MONUSCO.
Monusco has initiated its drawdown in view of eventually leaving the country. The JHRO branches will stay in many locations and will be one of the last offices to leave. I The grant will be a general support for the country programme however there will be some soft earmarking towards areas that Sweden wants to see prioritised.
The intervention will focus on the following objectives:
1. Strengthening rule of law and accountability for human rights violations 2. Enhancing and Protecting Civic Space and People’s Participation 3. Enhancing equality and countering discrimination - address leaving no one behind and root causes of inequality 4. Integrating human rights in sustainable development 5. Early warning, prevention and protection of HR in situations of conflict 6. Increasing implementation of the international human rights mechanisms

UNJHRO (JHRO) övervakar människorättssituationen i Demokratiska republiken Kongo och Sverige har stöttat dess arbete bilateralt sedan 2016 med två olika bidrag. Enligt ambassaden, och det internationella samfundet i stort i Demokratiska republiken Kongo, är JHRO den starkaste människorättsaktören i Kongo-Kinshasa och därför vill ambassaden stödja kontoret. JHRO är ett gemensamt kontor mellan OHCHR och människorättssektionen i Monusco-uppdraget i Demokratiska republiken Kongo. Dessutom har JHRO ett nära samarbete med UNDP för att tillhandahålla utbildning i mänskliga rättigheter till armén och polisen, och de är också nära kopplade till övertagandet av Monusco.
Monusco har inlett sin neddragning med sikte på att så småningom lämna landet. JHRO-filialerna kommer att stanna på många platser och kommer att vara ett av de sista kontoren som lämnar. Bidraget blir ett generellt stöd till landprogrammet men det blir en viss mjuk öronmärkning mot områden som Sverige vill se prioriterade.
Interventionen kommer att inriktas på följande mål:
1. Stärka rättsstatsprincipen och ansvarsskyldigheten för kränkningar av de mänskliga rättigheterna 2. Förbättra och skydda det medborgerliga utrymmet och människors deltagande 3. Ökad jämlikhet och motverkande av diskriminering – ta itu med att inte lämna någon på efterkälken och de bakomliggande orsakerna till ojämlikhet 4. Integrera mänskliga rättigheter i hållbar utveckling 5. Tidig varning, förebyggande och skydd av mänskliga rättigheter i konfliktsituationer 6. Ökat genomförande av de internationella mekanismerna för mänskliga rättigheter
